finding_key: .github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml::`allowed_bots` hardcodes the bot login "yorkie-agent[bot]", which is nowhere derived from or documented for the configured app — if the installed app's slug differs, the allow-list never matches and the fix step still fails
evidence: In the supplied workflows the App identity is only ever supplied through secrets (`secrets.AGENT_APP_ID` / `AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` in agent-review-panel.yml's "Generate GitHub App token" step and agent-iterate-ci.yml's equivalent), so nothing in the repo pins or validates the bot login; the new `allowed_bots: "yorkie-agent[bot],yorkie-agent"` at agent-review-panel.yml:413 and agent-iterate-ci.yml:160 is indeed an undocumented literal whose correctness depends on which App a deployer installed. The claim is therefore accurate about the code as written, and the suggested `steps.app-token.outputs.app-slug` derivation is a real output of actions/create-github-app-token@v1. It is a conditional/fragility defect rather than a demonstrated failure — the claim does not (and I cannot) show the actual installed slug differs, and the failure mode is fail-safe (the fix job reds and the newly-widened `stalled` job pages a human rather than silently doing nothing). I could not grep the repo (empty working directory), so I am relying on the supplied files and cannot independently confirm the reviewer's "no other occurrence of yorkie-agent" grep or the exact matching semantics of claude-code-action's `allowed_bots`.
